title: The Hares and the Frogs
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: The Hares once gathered together and lamented the unhappiness of their lot, exposed as they were to dangers on all sides and lacking the strength and the courage to hold their own. Men, dogs, birds and beasts of prey were all their enemies, and killed and devoured them daily: and sooner than endure such persecution any longer, they one and all determined to end their miserable lives.

Thus resolved and desperate, they rushed in a body towards a neighbouring pool, intending to drown themselves. On the bank were sitting a number of Frogs, who, when they heard the noise of the Hares as they ran, with one accord leaped into the water and hid themselves in the depths.

Then one of the older Hares who was wiser than the rest cried out to his companions, "Stop, my friends, take heart; don't let us destroy ourselves after all: see, here are creatures who are afraid of us, and who must, therefore, be still more timid than ourselves."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Hares lament about their lot?
options: Their lack of food during the winter months
Their small numbers compared to other animals
Their unhappiness, exposed to danger and lacking strength and courage
Their inability to find a safe place to sleep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which creatures are named as the Hares' enemies?
options: Men, dogs, birds and beasts of prey
Foxes, wolves, and eagles alone
Only the birds that hunt by day
Snakes, spiders, and other small creatures

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Hares decide to do rather than endure persecution any longer?
options: Move far away to a new land
Ask the other animals for mercy
Build a shelter to hide in
End their miserable lives

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Frogs do when they hear the Hares approaching?
options: They freeze in place, too frightened to move
They leap into the water and hide in the depths
They call out a warning to other frogs
They hop away into the tall grass

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the older Hare tell his companions to do?
options: Keep running until they reach the pool
Choose a new leader among themselves
Stop and take heart, rather than destroy themselves
Search for a safer pool farther away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what reason does the older Hare give for his companions to stop?
options: The Frogs are afraid of them, so the Hares must not be the most timid creatures
The pool is too shallow to drown in safely
Another group of Hares has already been saved
The Frogs have offered to help them instead

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do the Hares originally head toward the pool?
options: They want to drink before continuing their journey
They are chasing the Frogs away from the bank
They hope to find safety from their enemies in the water
They intend to drown themselves there

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the sight of the fleeing Frogs teach the older Hare?
options: That the Frogs are secretly working with their enemies
That the Hares are not as powerless as they believed, since something fears them too
That the pool is too dangerous to enter at all
That the Hares should ask the Frogs for advice

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "lamented" mean in "lamented the unhappiness of their lot"?
options: Celebrated happily
Argued fiercely about
Expressed sorrow over
Forgot completely about

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: However bad your own situation seems, someone else may be worse off still
Frogs are naturally braver than hares in every situation
Giving up is always the wisest response to danger
Only the oldest members of a group can offer good advice

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how often are the Hares killed and devoured by their enemies?
options: Once a year
Only in winter
Rarely, but without warning
Daily

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where are the Frogs sitting before the Hares arrive?
options: Deep beneath the water
On the bank of the pool
Among the tall reeds nearby
On a fallen log by the water

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many of the Hares agree to end their lives?
options: Only a small group of the youngest Hares
Just the older Hares among them
They one and all determined to do so
None; they only discussed the idea

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the noise of the running Hares cause the Frogs to flee?
options: The Frogs mistake the approaching Hares for a threat to themselves
The Frogs recognize the Hares and want to greet them
The Frogs are fleeing from a separate predator nearby
The Frogs are following a signal from the older Hare

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the older Hare described as "wiser than the rest"?
options: He is the only one who knows the way to the pool
He has survived more attacks than any other Hare
He alone refuses to run toward the pool at all
He notices something the others overlook and uses it to change their minds

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "timid" mean in the older Hare's remark?
options: Quick to anger
Easily frightened
Physically weak
Unable to see well

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Hares successfully drown themselves in the pool
The Frogs teach the Hares how to defend themselves
Despairing Hares abandon their plan to drown themselves after seeing creatures more fearful than they are
The Hares and Frogs agree to share the pool peacefully
